sources.title: Human History Map, late Sinhalese records and decoded island outlines
sources.note: Own-project factual-data exception. Exact missing IDs 1279-1492 and 1492-1530, five decoded snapshots. Broad island shape includes Yapahuwa, Kurunegala, Gampola, Kotte and Kandy; clips coastal Colombo, Galle, Jaffna and Nallur test points. Related early Sinhalese cards remain separate.

sources.title: Central Cultural Fund, Yapahuwa Rock Fortress
sources.note: Institutional full page read through indexed original; direct URL times out. Exact query site:ccf.gov.lk Yapahuwa staircase reproduces full page. Used fortification, Tooth Relic, thirteenth-century carved stairway and rock cisterns. Capture placed in 1280s rather than exact disputed 1283/1284; no speculative Chinese architectural connection or unsupported emotional claims.

sources.title: Siddham IN03166, Gadaladeniya Rock-Inscription of Dharmmakirtti Sthavira, translated from Paranavitana
sources.note: Original scholarly database translation read directly, lines 5-12 for craftspeople/payment, 18-45 for endowments and reserved family usufruct. Date 28 April 1344 explained in introduction. Source edition is Epigraphia Zeylanica IV, no. 12; entire underlying work conservatively treated together if reused. No transcription from garbled OCR used.

sources.title: Siddham IN03212, Lankatilaka Rock Inscription of Bhuvanaikabahu IV, translations
sources.note: Original scholarly translation page directly read. Paranavitana 1960 lines 2-12 for patron family and payment; Gunasekara 1887 longer translation includes new dam, land, 200 unfree male/female workers and 400 cattle/buffaloes, households paying one fanam. Tamil counterpart IN03214 independently corroborates unfree labor and annual household paṇam; counted as same underlying inscription-study work, not extra source budget. No literal modern currency conversion or preserved original four-storey building claim.

sources.title: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte Municipal Council, History
sources.note: Original municipal history read directly. Used Alakeshwara fort geography, Kolonna/Diyawanna waterways, early fifteenth-century court and monarch list through Dharmapala in 1597. Text repeatedly misnumbers Parakramabahu VI as IV, so detailed royal acts/kinship and precise later succession list not adopted. Broader historical chronology compared with Codrington.

sources.title: H. W. Codrington, A Short History of Ceylon, chapter VI (1926), digital edition
sources.note: Public-domain historical work read directly via digital edition. Used 1521 partition paragraph and discussion of Jaffna/Kandy distinctness; source chronology and dynastic kinship often disputed, so no exact fifteenth-century accession, prejudice about peoples, or genetic/ethnic inference adopted. Edition and source date explicit.

sources.title: Dharshani Lakmali Jayasinghe, Translating Worlds through Words: The Bird-View of the Selalihini Sandeshaya (2022)
sources.note: Original Stanford Humanities Center/Dibur scholar-translator essay read directly. Opening dates composition about 1450 and monk’s Vijayabahu Pirivena leadership; paragraphs on verse 22 and 73-75 for Tamil hymns/women performing; verse 7 commentary explicitly prints සුරපුර and gloss city of gods/heaven/celestial city. Sample modern Sinhala type, not medieval autograph. Avoided article’s questionable political generalizations, modern capital description and Naga historical speculation.

sources.title: Zoltán Biedermann, city of Colombo, Encyclopaedia of Portuguese Expansion (2009)
sources.note: Original university-hosted scholarly entry read directly. Circa 1500 exports/imports, 1518 fort, 1524 dismantling, 1528 request and 1565 court relocation. Source has erroneous Dharmapala 1594 death and geographic southeast phrasing, excluded; ending in 1597 supplied separately by monarch list. Early Portuguese arrival date not selected because sources vary 1505/1506.

sources.title: Chandra Richard de Silva, Trade in Ceylon Cinnamon in the Sixteenth Century
sources.note: Original University of Peradeniya repository PDF indexed text read, printed page 21, paragraphs on 1520 Crown monopoly, 1524 routing rule and 1521 prices. Direct file times out. Full-title query with 1524 returns original page text. Publication upload date not treated as original article date. No 1533 terms projected into 1520s.

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Trilingual Inscription (TribhashaSellipiya)
sources.note: Original institutional page read directly: date 1409, Chinese/Persian/Tamil, Zheng He, 1911 discovery, current Colombo original/Galle replica. Erection day not equated with inscribed date; external Chinese-sponsored object and clipped coastal findspot made explicit.

proposedOverrides.summary: Late medieval Sri Lanka across changing royal centers and the Kotte period. These broad atlas outlines do not establish continuous island-wide rule or one uniform population.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One shared late-medieval regional umbrella across consecutive atlas phases, not an unchanged state
batchIdentityNotes.geography: Five broad island polygons. Yapahuwa/Kurunegala/Gampola/Gadaladeniya/Lankatilaka/Kotte/Kandy/Anuradhapura included; coastal Colombo/Galle/Jaffna/Nallur points excluded by simplification. No correction to runtime geometry proposed.
batchIdentityNotes.distinct: Existing simhala and sinhalese-kingdoms (800-900) remain separate. Named Kandy and colonial Ceylon records not associated. Tamil Jaffna never reduced to generic Sinhala culture or permanent Kotte district. Local effective power differs from island outline.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Original intervals retained. Period 1415 boundary conventional Kotte inauguration, not exact founding of all institutions. Yapahuwa loss only in the 1280s; later 1521 partition has contemporaneous phase treatment. Post-1530 history clearly later.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Original Sinhala word සුරපුර in scholar’s modern-type discussion of fifteenth-century Selalihini Sandeshaya verse 7; clear source gloss and no autograph claim.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Primary grants support agricultural water, household obligations, elite family donation and unfree labor. No securely attributed medieval household toilets, universal formal schooling or local medical protocol established; no older Anuradhapura hospital projected forward.
